faq.question: How does Cagrilintide complement GLP-1 receptor agonists?
faq.answer: Cagrilintide targets the amylin pathway (AMY-R) via the area postrema, producing distinct effects: delayed gastric emptying, reduced postprandial glucagon, and central appetite modulation. GLP-1 agonists target GLP-1R in the hypothalamus and GI tract. Together, they engage two independent satiety and nutrient-processing pathways — this is the basis for dual-pathway research protocols.

faq.question: How does Cagrilintide compare to other amylin analogues?
faq.answer: Cagrilintide is a long-acting acylated amylin analogue engineered for extended half-life via C20 fatty acid conjugation. Compared to native amylin (t½ ~13 min) or pramlintide (t½ ~50 min), Cagrilintide's structural modifications confer significantly longer residence time, enabling once-weekly dosing in research protocols.
